(By Sri. Yogesh D. Nayak, Hcgp)

THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO a) DIRECT THE RESPONDENT AUTHORITIES TO CONSIDER THE PETITIONER'S REPRESENTATIONS EFFECTIVELY MADE ON 30/06/2023 FOR GRANT OF COMPENSATION FOR THE ACQUIRED LAND AT LAND BEARING NO. 558, SITUATED AT GRAMATANA, KASABA HOBLI, HASSAN, MEASURING 15 X 6.5 SQ.FT., IN TOTAL 97.50 SQ.FT., PRODUCED AS ANNEXURE-A,
B AND C AND ETC.

THESE WRIT PETITIONS ARE COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard Ms.Swathi G, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. Yogesh D.Nayak, learned HCGP for the respondents.
NC: 2023:KHC:33307 WP No. 20479 of 2023 AND WP NO.20522 of 2023 2.
These writ petitions put in issue common facts, questions and reliefs to be considered.

3. Case of the petitioner in W.P.No.20479/2023 is that she is the absolute owner of the property bearing No.1493, (old No.1844) situated at Gramatana, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan, measuring 15 X 6.5 sq.ft. consisting of RCC building measuring 97.50 sq.ft. out of the land measuring 15X50 sq.ft.,
totally measuring 750 sq.ft.,having purchased the same in terms of a deed of sale as per Annexure-F.
4.

Case of the petitioner in W.P.No.20522/2023 is that he is the absolute owner of land bearing No.558, situated at Gramatana, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan, measuring 15 X 6.5 sq.ft. consisting of RCC building measuring 97.50 sq.ft. out of the land measuring 15X50 sq.ft., totally measuring 750 sq.ft.,
having purchased the same in terms of a deed of sale as per Annexure-F.

sentences.text:
It is the case of the petitioners that their lands have been utilized by the respondent-authorities for the purpose of widening of B.M.Road (Bangalore-Mangalore road), Hassan without acquiring the same in a manner known to law.
6.

It is further case of the petitioners that having utilised the lands for the purpose of widening of the road, Government has now issued a Notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 as per Annexure-G.
Petitioners are therefore before this Court seeking compensation in respect of their lands which have already been utilized.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners apart from reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of petitions also relies upon the order dated 22.02.2021 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.50178/2019 c/w W.P.No.181/2020 in respect of the very same notification pertaining to one Sri. H.V. NC: 2023:KHC:33307 WP No. 20479 of 2023 AND WP NO.20522 of 2023 Ramanaraju directing the respondent-authorities to initiate and complete the acquisition process and to pass award and disburse the compensation and the entire process/ procedure was directed to be completed within a period, not later than twelve weeks from the date of release of the order and liberty was reserved to the petitioners to seek remedy with regard to quantum of compensation if not satisfied with the award, in terms of Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
8.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners further relies upon another order dated 19.06.2023 passed in W.P.No.10651/2023 by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of one H.S.Yathiraj who was also similarly situated with that of the petitioners.

In which, apart from taking note of earlier order dated 22.02.2021, this Court had also directed to the respondent-authorities to take into consideration the order passed in LAC No.28/2010 in NC: 2023:KHC:33307 WP No. 20479 of 2023 AND WP NO.20522 of 2023 respect of claim made by persons similarly situated to that of the petitioners while determining the compensation.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioners therefore submits that respondents may be directed to consider the case of the petitioners in the lines of the orders passed in the aforesaid writ petitions.

10. Learned AGA while admitting the aforesaid position with regard to utilization of the lands of the petitioners and also issuance of subsequent notification and also with regard to the orders passed by this court submits that case of the petitioners would be considered on its merits and if they found entitled to the compensation, necessary orders would be passed.
11.
Taking note of the said submissions, these petitions are disposed of.

The respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 5 shall complete the process as directed in the order passed by this Court in W.P.No.50178/2019 c/w W.P.No.181/2020 NC: 2023:KHC:33307 WP No. 20479 of 2023 AND WP NO.20522 of 2023 and also shall take note of the order passed in W.P.No.10651/2023 dated 19.06.2023 while determining the case of the petitioners and the said process shall be completed within a period of twelve (12) weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.

All contentions are kept open either with regard to quantum of enhancement of compensation or the clarification required by the petitioners.
Accordingly, writ petitions are disposed of.
